summary.name: 拾音 Shiyin
summary.one_liner: Shiyin (拾音) is a free, open-source Mac meeting recorder that transcribes audio on-device, separates speakers, and produces timestamped meeting notes.
use_cases: Recording and transcribing Zoom, Meet or Teams calls without a bot
Turning meeting audio into structured notes with decisions and action items
Transcribing mixed Chinese and English meetings
Transcribing existing audio or video files
Searching past meetings by asking questions with timestamped answers
summary.what_it_does: Records microphone and computer audio on a Mac, showing a live transcript while recording and re-transcribing on-device after stopping. It separates speakers, lets the user rename them, and remembers voices for future meetings. Notes, summaries, decisions, to-dos and open questions are generated from the transcript, with timestamps that jump to the audio. Transcription and speaker identification run locally; only text is sent to a chosen AI tool (Claude Code, Codex, Anthropic or OpenAI API) when organizing or asking questions. It can also import srt, vtt or txt transcripts and transcribe dragged-in audio or video files.
notable: Records Zoom, Meet and Teams audio without adding a meeting bot
Transcription and speaker identification run on-device; audio is not uploaded
Tuned for Taiwanese Mandarin and Chinese-English code-switching using Breeze ASR 25
Timestamped notes link back to the recording; MIT-licensed open source
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later and Apple Silicon (M1 or newer), 8 GB RAM minimum
Transcription model is about 1.7 GB downloaded on first use; Japanese model is an extra ~570 MB
Not signed with an Apple developer certificate, so macOS blocks first launch and needs manual approval in Privacy & Security settings
